TokenSave Language Tax Index

The “language tax” is how many more tokens the same text needs in your language than in English. On today's models the median across 40 languages is +41% on Gemini, +52% on GPT and +88% on Claude 5.5 (Opus, Sonnet and Haiku). API prices, context windows and token-based limits all scale with it.

What the index shows

  • Every model taxes non-English text, but by very different amounts. Gemini has the smallest median tax, Claude the largest. Korean is +41% on Gemini, +44% on GPT and +89% on Claude 5.5; Ukrainian +74%, +88% and +70%.
  • The tax has fallen over time. On the legacy GPT-4 tokenizer (cl100k) the median was +129%; on the current o200k tokenizer it is +52%. Hindi went from +359% to +50%.
  • A lower tax is not always a cheaper model. The index compares each language with English on the same model. Claude 5.5 also needs more tokens for English itself (47 for our prompt, against 34 on GPT and 34 on Gemini), and prices per token differ. Use the token calculator to compare real costs.
  • New in v1.1: Haiku 5.5 has a smaller tax than Haiku 4.5, because English got more expensive. Haiku 5.5 counts exactly like Opus and Sonnet 5.5 in all 41 languages. Its median tax is +88% against +108% on Haiku 4.5, but no language got cheaper: English rose from 35 to 47 tokens (+34%), Spanish +41% and German +42%, while Korean (89), Japanese, Chinese, Hindi, Russian and Ukrainian stayed exactly the same. Across all 41 prompts Haiku 5.5 uses 9% more tokens. At list prices ($0.10 vs $1 per million input tokens) it is still far cheaper per prompt.
  • It matters most for chat, documents and API work, much less for coding agents. In our coding test the prompt language moved input tokens by about 1%, because the agent's own instructions dwarf the prompt (data).

Method

  • Definition: tax = tokens for the language ÷ tokens for English on the same tokenizer − 1, rounded to a whole percent. The headline number is the median over the 40 non-English languages.
  • Text: one everyday instruction (summarize a customer email and suggest a reply) translated into 41 languages. The prompts and raw counts are in the two source datasets: GPT tokenizers (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23427148) and Claude, Gemini and GPT (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428350).
  • Counting: GPT with tiktoken; Claude from Claude Code usage reports minus a one-character baseline; Gemini with the Google AI Studio token counter. Models that share a tokenizer share a column (Claude Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5 gave identical counts in all 41 languages, as did Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.1 Pro).

Update policy and version history

We re-measure the same 41 prompts when a model with a new tokenizer ships, add or replace its column, and publish a new version here with the date. Earlier versions stay in the history, so changes over time can be cited.

  • v1.1 · 2026-10-20 · Added Claude Haiku 5.5 (released 2026-10-07), measured on all 41 prompts: identical counts to Opus and Sonnet 5.5 in every language, so it joins the Claude 5.5 column. Versus Haiku 4.5, English needs 34% more tokens (35 to 47) while Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Hindi, Russian and Ukrainian are unchanged.
  • v1.0 · 2026-10-19 · First release: 41 languages × 4 current tokenizers plus the legacy GPT-4 tokenizer, from our 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-17 measurements.

Queued for the next version: none.

Limitations

  • The index rests on one prompt. On other text the per-language numbers move by roughly ±10–20 percentage points; the ranking of models and languages is more stable. Adding more texts is planned for a later version.
  • Input tokens only. Output in another language can cost more again, and prices per token differ by model.
  • Claude counts come from usage reports and can be off by about ±2 tokens.
